parameters.query:
-- Claim a batch of unresearched companies, subject to the per-domain fetch
-- rate limit. FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED means two overlapping runs take different
-- rows instead of fighting over the same ones, which is the pattern
-- n8n/README.md mandates for every queue read.
--
-- The rate limit is applied at claim time rather than at fetch time, and it is
-- the reason the pool is read wider than the batch: a company whose domain is
-- still cooling down is not claimed at all, so it stays at 'new' and the next
-- pass takes it, and a company behind it in the queue gets the slot instead.
-- Filtering after claiming would leave rows stranded at 'researching'.
--
-- claim_domain_fetch (0012_fetch_throttle.sql) both tests and stamps in one
-- statement, so two concurrent runs cannot both decide a domain is free. It is
-- volatile, so the planner evaluates it per row as the LIMIT pulls them: a
-- domain that is never reached is never stamped.
--
-- prior_failures is counted from agent_runs rather than from a column on
-- companies: the audit trail already knows how many times research failed for
-- this company, so there is no need for a retry counter and no migration.
WITH candidates AS (
    SELECT id, domain
    FROM companies
    WHERE status = 'new'
    ORDER BY created_at
    LIMIT ($1::jsonb ->> 'candidate_pool')::int
    FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
),
allowed AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM candidates
    WHERE claim_domain_fetch(
              domain,
              make_interval(mins => ($1::jsonb ->> 'domain_cooldown_minutes')::int)
          )
    LIMIT ($1::jsonb ->> 'batch_size')::int
),
claimed AS (
    UPDATE companies
    SET status = 'researching'
    WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM allowed)
    RETURNING id, name, domain, website, industry
)
SELECT c.id            AS company_id,
       c.name,
       c.domain::text  AS domain,
       c.website,
       c.industry,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM agent_runs r
         WHERE r.company_id = c.id
           AND r.agent_name = 'research'
           AND r.status = 'error')::int AS prior_failures
FROM claimed c;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ batch_size: Number($env.RESEARCH_BATCH_SIZE || 5), candidate_pool: Number($env.RESEARCH_CANDIDATE_POOL || 25), domain_cooldown_minutes: Number($env.RESEARCH_DOMAIN_COOLDOWN_MINUTES || 60) } ) }}

nodes.name: Claim Companies
nodes.notes: Claims only companies whose domain is outside its fetch cooldown. A throttled company stays at 'new' and waits for the next pass.

nodes.name: Fetch robots.txt
nodes.notes: A missing robots.txt means no restrictions were published, which is allow.

nodes.name: Allowed URLs
nodes.notes: Longest-match wins between Allow and Disallow, per RFC 9309.

nodes.name: Split URLs
nodes.notes: Fan out to one item per allowed page.

nodes.name: Fetch Page
nodes.notes: One request at a time by default, spaced by RESEARCH_FETCH_BATCH_INTERVAL_MS. domain_fetch_log is the limit between runs; this is the limit inside one.

nodes.name: Group Material
nodes.notes: Fan back in to one item per company. HTML to text, capped.

parameters.query:
-- Triage is an LLM call, so it leaves its own agent_runs row. agent_name is
-- 'classifier' because that is what this is: a cheap local filter, which is the
-- role agents/README.md assigns to the local model.
INSERT INTO agent_runs (agent_name, company_id, input, status, model, started_at)
VALUES (
    'classifier',
    ($1::jsonb ->> 'company_id')::uuid,
    $1::jsonb -> 'input',
    'running',
    $1::jsonb ->> 'model',
    now()
)
RETURNING id, company_id, status;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ company_id: $json.company_id, model: $env.OLLAMA_MODEL || 'llama3.1:8b', input: { execution_id: String($execution.id), workflow_id: $workflow.id, stage: 'triage', company: $json.name, domain: $json.domain, pages_fetched: $json.pages_fetched, material_chars: $json.material_chars } } ) }}

nodes.name: Build Triage Request
nodes.notes: Short prompt, 4000 characters of material, 256 output tokens. Triage runs for every company, so its cost is paid every time.

nodes.name: Triage
nodes.notes: Local Ollama. No credential: Ollama has no authentication and the base URL is configuration, not a secret.

nodes.name: Validate Triage
nodes.notes: Fails open. A broken filter must cost money, never silently discard leads.

parameters.query:
-- Close the triage run and carry the verdict forward as a column, so the IF
-- after this node reads its own input instead of reaching back across the
-- branch for it.
WITH closed AS (
    UPDATE agent_runs
    SET status      = 'success',
        output      = $1::jsonb -> 'output',
        error       = NULL,
        finished_at = now()
    WHERE id = ($1::jsonb ->> 'triage_run_id')::uuid
    RETURNING id
)
SELECT (SELECT id FROM closed)                      AS triage_run_id,
       ($1::jsonb ->> 'worth_researching')::boolean AS worth_researching,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'company_id'                   AS company_id,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'name'                         AS name,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'domain'                       AS domain,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'triage_reason'                AS triage_reason;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ triage_run_id: $json.triage_run_id, company_id: $json.company_id, name: $json.name, domain: $json.domain, worth_researching: $json.worth_researching, triage_reason: $json.triage_reason, output: { worth_researching: $json.worth_researching, reason: $json.triage_reason, evidence_seen: $json.triage_evidence, failed_open: $json.triage_failed_open, model: $json.triage_model } } ) }}

parameters.query:
-- Triage found nothing worth paying the research model for. The company is
-- parked rather than deleted, and the reason is on its classifier run in
-- agent_runs. Setting status back to 'new' re-queues it.
UPDATE companies
SET status = 'ignored'
WHERE id = ($1::jsonb ->> 'company_id')::uuid
  AND status = 'researching'
RETURNING id, name, domain::text AS domain, status;

nodes.name: Park Company
nodes.notes: Skipped by triage. Re-queue by setting status back to 'new'.

parameters.query:
-- Bracket the run: 'running' before the model call, terminal after.
-- company_id is set here, which is what lets WF-101 and v_agent_health attribute
-- a failure to a company later.
INSERT INTO agent_runs (agent_name, company_id, input, status, model, started_at)
VALUES (
    'research',
    ($1::jsonb ->> 'company_id')::uuid,
    $1::jsonb -> 'input',
    'running',
    $1::jsonb ->> 'model',
    now()
)
RETURNING id, company_id, status, started_at;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ company_id: $json.company_id, model: $env.OLLAMA_RESEARCH_MODEL || 'qwen9-64k:latest', input: { execution_id: String($execution.id), workflow_id: $workflow.id, stage: 'research', company: $json.name, domain: $json.domain, sources: $('Group Material').item.json.sources, fetch_failures: $('Group Material').item.json.fetch_failures, robots_blocked: $('Group Material').item.json.robots_blocked, material_chars: $('Group Material').item.json.material_chars, material_truncated: $('Group Material').item.json.material_truncated } } ) }}

nodes.name: Validate Research
nodes.notes: Drives every check off agents/research/schema.json; also catches truncation.

parameters.query:
-- Write the research and its evidence in one statement, so a company is never
-- left marked 'researched' with no signals because a second query failed.
--
-- signals has a unique index on (company_id, signal_type, md5(signal));
-- ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING makes re-running this workflow idempotent at the
-- database level rather than by workflow discipline.
WITH payload AS (
    SELECT $1::jsonb AS p
),
upd AS (
    UPDATE companies c
    SET description    = COALESCE(NULLIF(payload.p #>> '{analysis,company_summary}', ''), c.description),
        tech_stack     = COALESCE(payload.p #> '{analysis,technology}', c.tech_stack),
        hiring_signals = COALESCE(payload.p #> '{analysis,hiring_signals}', c.hiring_signals),
        pain_signals   = COALESCE(payload.p #> '{analysis,pain_signals}', c.pain_signals),
        status         = 'researched'
    FROM payload
    WHERE c.id = (payload.p ->> 'company_id')::uuid
      AND c.status = 'researching'
    RETURNING c.id
),
ins AS (
    INSERT INTO signals (company_id, signal_type, signal, source_url, confidence)
    SELECT (payload.p ->> 'company_id')::uuid,
           s ->> 'signal_type',
           s ->> 'signal',
           NULLIF(s ->> 'source', ''),
           COALESCE((s ->> 'confidence')::numeric, 0.50)
    FROM payload, jsonb_array_elements(payload.p -> 'signals') s
    ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
    RETURNING id
)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM upd)::int AS companies_updated,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM ins)::int AS signals_inserted,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'company_id'      AS company_id,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'agent_run_id'    AS agent_run_id;

nodes.name: Store Research
nodes.notes: companies and signals in one statement.

parameters.query:
-- Close the run and record what the call cost. agent_runs.duration_ms is a
-- generated column, so it falls out of finished_at on its own.
UPDATE agent_runs
SET status        = 'success',
    output        = $1::jsonb -> 'output',
    error         = NULL,
    prompt_tokens = ($1::jsonb #>> '{usage,prompt_tokens}')::int,
    output_tokens = ($1::jsonb #>> '{usage,completion_tokens}')::int,
    finished_at   = now()
WHERE id = ($1::jsonb ->> 'agent_run_id')::uuid
RETURNING id, company_id, status, prompt_tokens, output_tokens, duration_ms;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ agent_run_id: $('Validate Research').item.json.agent_run_id, usage: $('Validate Research').item.json.usage, output: { validated: true, warnings: $('Validate Research').item.json.warnings, analysis: $('Validate Research').item.json.analysis, raw_response: $('Validate Research').item.json.raw_response, signals_inserted: $json.signals_inserted } } ) }}

parameters.query:
-- Close the run as failed and hand the company back to the queue.
--
-- After three failures the company is parked at 'ignored' rather than cycling
-- forever: a site that cannot be researched twice is unlikely to become
-- researchable on the fourth attempt, and an infinite retry loop burns tokens.
-- prior_failures is the count from before this run, so >= 2 means this is the
-- third.
--
-- The company is only moved if it is still 'researching'. If something else
-- already advanced it, this workflow does not drag it backwards.
WITH closed AS (
    UPDATE agent_runs
    SET status      = 'error',
        error       = COALESCE(NULLIF($1::jsonb ->> 'error', ''), 'Research failed with no message'),
        output      = $1::jsonb -> 'output',
        finished_at = now()
    WHERE id = ($1::jsonb ->> 'agent_run_id')::uuid
    RETURNING id, company_id
),
requeued AS (
    UPDATE companies c
    SET status = CASE WHEN ($1::jsonb ->> 'prior_failures')::int >= 2 THEN 'ignored' ELSE 'new' END
    FROM closed
    WHERE c.id = closed.company_id
      AND c.status = 'researching'
    RETURNING c.id, c.status
)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM closed)::int              AS runs_closed,
       (SELECT status FROM requeued)                   AS company_status,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'company_id'                      AS company_id,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'error'                           AS error;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ agent_run_id: $json.agent_run_id, company_id: $json.company_id, prior_failures: $json.prior_failures, error: $json.error_message, output: { validated: false, errors: $json.errors, raw_response: $json.raw_response } } ) }}

nodes.name: Close Run Error
nodes.notes: Closes the run and returns the company to the queue, or parks it at 'ignored' after three failures.
